etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Doll, a popular pet form of Dorothy.

definitions.definition: A toy in the form of a human.

quote.text: Some fine day we may have the country raised, and the gendarmes down upon us from Strasburg, and all owing to your pretty doll, with her cunning ways of coming over you.

definitions.definition: (US, Australia, dated) A term of endearment: darling, sweetheart.

quote.text: "They didn't sell cigarettes where you were, doll?" Palmer asked.

definitions.definition: (US, dated) A good-natured, cooperative or helpful girl.

quote.text: Ow! These things are defective. Pipsqueak, be a doll, I need a new pair, pronto!

definitions.definition: The smallest or pet pig in a litter.
A kind of barrier used in horse racing.

quote.citation: 1885, William Day, The Racehorse in Training, page 87:
quote.text: On a beautiful spring morning, after the “dolls and chains” had been removed to allow the horses room to pass through, in galloping “across the flat,”  […]

definitions.definition: (rail transport) A short signal post mounted on a bracket mounted on the main signal post, or on a signal gantry.

quote.citation: 1943 March and April, “Notes and News: Peculiar Distant Signals on L.N.E.R”, in Railway Magazine, page 116:
quote.text: The signals are on a three-doll bracket post; one doll carries two [signal] arms, one above the other.

quote.citation: 1966, Jacqueline Susann, Valley of the Dolls, page 227:
quote.text: Each night she looked at the bottle of Seconals with affection. She never could do this without the dolls. She would have spent sleepless nights, smoking, worrying—and she would have lost her nerve.
